beats.narration_slice: Families and customs teach rules about modesty.
beats.visual: Mineral fresco of an ancestral family group beside a cave hearth as an elder gently draws a hide wrap around a younger figure, with simple ochre gesture marks suggesting learned imitation rather than written rules.
beats.purpose: show modesty norms being socially taught within families and customs
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium-wide family hearth scene; elder actively demonstrates a hide covering to a younger figure; side-on composition beneath warm firelight; clustered ancestral silhouettes and hanging hides
beats.continuity: begins the subject world independently from the opener, grounding the explanation in learned social behavior

beats.narration_slice: Those rules vary across cultures and history.
beats.visual: Wide limestone fresco showing a winding procession across three ancient architectural zones, with different groups using distinct combinations of draped textile, hide, ornament, and uncovered stylized silhouettes, all rendered without text.
beats.purpose: show that modesty conventions differ between societies and historical periods
beats.visual_fingerprint: very wide processional panorama; multiple cultural groups walking through cave shelter, columned courtyard, and stone settlement zones; varied coverings and symbolic motifs; horizontal journey composition
beats.continuity: expands from one family's learned custom to visibly different conventions across places and eras

beats.narration_slice: Chosen privacy differs from unexpected exposure.
beats.visual: Top-down ochre fresco of one stylized figure calmly stepping behind a suspended hide partition while, elsewhere in the same simple scene, another figure recoils as a separate partition is suddenly pulled aside by wind.
beats.purpose: contrast voluntary privacy with unwanted or surprising exposure
beats.visual_fingerprint: high-angle privacy scene; two spatially separated figures with opposite reactions; one deliberately enters concealment while another is unexpectedly revealed by a lifted hide; diagonal partition composition
beats.continuity: moves from broad social variation to the individual's control over who can see the body

beats.narration_slice: Context can also make nudity feel sexual.
beats.visual: Close mineral-fresco view of two non-explicit adult silhouettes at the edge of an intimate curtained sleeping alcove, surrounded by subtle paired ochre motifs and warmer terracotta pigment, making the setting—not anatomy—the dominant cue.
beats.purpose: show how an intimate setting can give nudity sexual meaning
beats.visual_fingerprint: close two-person adult silhouette scene; curtained sleeping alcove; warm terracotta emphasis and paired symbolic motifs; compressed intimate composition with no explicit anatomy
beats.continuity: shifts from control of visibility to how surrounding circumstances alter interpretation of the same bodily state

beats.narration_slice: Expected staring or judgment can trigger shame.
beats.visual: Low-angle charcoal-and-ochre fresco of a lone figure curling inward and covering their torso while several distant faces appear only as dark eye-like silhouettes along a cave ledge, all gazes converging toward the central person.
beats.purpose: show anticipated scrutiny and judgment producing a shame response
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle isolated figure; hunched self-covering posture; distant semicircle of staring silhouettes above; converging charcoal gaze marks and strong empty stone around the subject
beats.continuity: turns from contextual sexual meaning to the emotional effect of believing others are watching and judging

beats.narration_slice: Galleries may present nude statues as ordinary art.
beats.visual: Frontal fresco of a simplified classical nude marble statue on a stone plinth inside an ancient gallery-like colonnade, with relaxed visitors calmly passing on either side and no one reacting with alarm.
beats.purpose: show a setting where the nude body is conventionally framed as ordinary art
beats.visual_fingerprint: symmetrical frontal gallery composition; pale classical statue centered on plinth; calm passing visitors; columned stone setting and cooler limestone-dominant pigment balance
beats.continuity: provides a contrasting social context in which visible nudity attracts routine aesthetic attention rather than personal judgment

beats.narration_slice: Changing booths usually signal concealment from strangers.
beats.visual: Oblique mineral-fresco view down a row of primitive textile changing stalls, with one person fully hidden behind a closed hide curtain while anonymous passersby remain outside the partitioned space.
beats.purpose: show that changing spaces conventionally communicate privacy from strangers
beats.visual_fingerprint: oblique corridor perspective; repeating hide-and-textile booths receding into depth; one firmly closed curtain as focal object; strangers kept outside the concealed interior
beats.continuity: contrasts the open gallery with a setting whose physical design explicitly signals expected concealment

beats.narration_slice: The skin stays ordinary; the social meaning changes.
beats.visual: Single central human silhouette painted in neutral ochre on bare limestone while surrounding contextual symbols form a loose ring: family hearth, hide curtain, watching eyes, intimate alcove motif, statue plinth, and changing partition, emphasizing that the body itself remains unchanged.
beats.purpose: summarize that shame comes from changing social meaning and context rather than from skin itself
beats.visual_fingerprint: centered solitary unchanged body silhouette; circular constellation of six contextual symbols around it; flat symbolic limestone field; balanced summary composition with no surrounding crowd
beats.continuity: synthesizes the preceding family, privacy, sexuality, judgment, gallery, and changing-space examples into the promised explanation
